archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A veteran mobile passer whose legs still add real value when plays break down, even though designed runs no longer work, paired with a short, conservative passing diet and a long-standing habit of taking sacks.

report.headline: His throws are fine; sacks and a timid aerial plan are sinking the offense
report.take:
Watson's 2026 is a partial rebound, not a revival. The Houston version (2018-2020) was an efficient downfield passer with top-10 EPA and CPOE marks. The Cleveland version bottomed out in 2024 at -0.229 EPA per play, 54th of 60. Under Todd Monken he is back near the middle of the pack: 7.25 yards per attempt (18th), a +0.04 CPOE and a low 1.2% interception rate. On a per-throw basis this is a functional NFL quarterback.

The drag is everything around the throws. His 11.7% sack rate ranks 44th of 47, and the 17-game pace is 70 sacks. That is not all new. Even in his best Houston years his pressure-to-sack rate ranked around 40th of 54-59, so taking sacks has always been part of how he plays. What is new is the line in front of him. Cleveland's offense allows the highest hit rate in the league (32nd of 32), and the run game ranks 27th in EPA. A sack-prone holder behind the league's leakiest protection creates long third downs. On those he converts just 28.4% with -0.184 EPA per play and has taken 10 sacks. His passing EPA total is -4.6. His dropbacks come out at -0.8 only because his scrambles have been genuinely good.

The passing profile also hides something. When he throws 10+ air yards, he averages +0.446 EPA per attempt: +0.466 at intermediate and +0.419 deep. Throws under 10 yards produce only +0.056, and throws behind the line are negative. Yet his aggressiveness is 13.25%, his intended air yards are 7.39, and he throws two yards short of the sticks on average. The offense keeps choosing the low-value layer. Part of that is protection, since you check down when the edge collapses. Part of it looks like design and caution. Harold Fannin Jr. at +0.34 EPA per target is the clear best option and should be featured more.

The recent stretch shows the tension. Over the last three games his yardage climbed to 265.3 a game with a +3 CPOE. But his EPA per dropback fell to -0.075 and he threw zero touchdowns. Week 8 at Pittsburgh summed him up: 324 yards, 8 sacks, no touchdowns and a lost fumble. He is moving the ball between the 20s and giving it back through sacks and stalled drives.

strengths.title: Efficient when he pushes downfield
strengths.body: Throws of 10+ air yards return +0.446 EPA per attempt, and the intermediate band is his best area at +0.466. The completion rate is low, as expected on longer throws, but the payoff per attempt is far higher than his short game. The deep sample is only 27 attempts, so the exact figure will move. His Houston-era downfield efficiency suggests the skill is real rather than a fluke.

strengths.title: Scrambles rescue broken plays
strengths.body: His 24 scrambles average +0.433 EPA and have produced 9 first downs. That is why his dropback total sits near break-even despite the sacks. It is the reward side of holding the ball and extending plays. His 4th-ranked rushing yardage among QBs comes from this, not from the playbook: designed runs sit at -0.399 EPA with a 35% stuff rate.

strengths.title: Avoids the interception
strengths.body: A 1.2% interception rate ranks 12th of 47, against a 2.3% league average. The short-heavy, under-the-sticks approach costs explosiveness but limits picks. This is a stable floor as long as the conservative plan holds.

concerns.title: Sacks: his habit, the line's failure
concerns.body: An 11.7% sack rate (44th) and a 37.9% pressure-to-sack rate are the main reason his EPA per dropback ranks 29th. His career shows he has always converted pressure into sacks at a high rate, so this will not disappear. It is magnified by a line allowing the league's highest hit rate. Expect it to persist unless the protection changes, because neither cause is a fluke.

concerns.title: Third downs stall out
concerns.body: Sacks and a 27th-ranked run game leave him facing an average of 8.4 yards to go on third down. There he converts only 28.4%, with -0.184 EPA per play and a -6.7 CPOE. Throwing two yards short of the sticks on average doesn't help. This is mostly a product of situation and scheme, and it is where drives die.

concerns.title: Fumbles and a touchdown drought
concerns.body: He has lost 3 fumbles (43rd of 47) and has 7 turnover-worthy fumbles, a cost of holding the ball in a collapsing pocket. Meanwhile his TD rate has gone to 0% over the last three games. His red-zone accuracy (+6.6 CPOE there) argues the drought is partly bad luck. The fumble risk, by contrast, follows the sacks and should stay.

trend.note: Yards have trended up (265.3 a game over the last three) while efficiency has slid: EPA per dropback is -0.062 over the last five and -0.075 over the last three, against -0.016 for the season. The 8-sack games against the Jets and Pittsburgh bookend that dip.

nextGame.headline: Saints' leaky deep coverage invites Watson to finally throw downfield
nextGame.body:
New Orleans is the softest pass defense he has seen in a while. It ranks 23rd in pass EPA, 31st in success rate, 27th in explosive passes allowed and 31st against deep throws. That matches the one part of his game that works: throws past 10 yards. The Saints also generate few hits (26th in hit rate), which matters most against the league's most porous line. They still finish well when they do get home, ranking 11th in sack rate. The game is indoors, and the 43.5 total is higher than any Browns game this season, with Cleveland a 2.5-point underdog.

Cleveland has no offensive injuries listed, so Watson gets his full group, Fannin included. On the Saints' side, safety Justin Reid (93% of snaps) is questionable after a concussion. If he sits, a deep secondary that is already struggling gets thinner. Defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd (illness, 66% of snaps) is also questionable, a modest interior pass-rush factor. The Saints' offensive injuries matter only for game script.

keyMatchups.title: Downfield shots vs. a broken deep secondary
keyMatchups.body: The Saints allow +1.251 EPA on deep throws, 31st in the league. Watson has been efficient beyond 10 yards but rarely goes there. If Monken lets him push the ball, this is the week the low aggressiveness rate should rise. If he keeps checking down, the matchup goes to waste.

keyMatchups.title: Leaky line vs. a light rush
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland allows the league's worst hit rate, while New Orleans ranks 26th at producing hits. That is the best protection setup he has had. It should mean fewer drive-killing sacks and cleaner chances to hold the ball for intermediate throws.

keyMatchups.title: Fannin against a TE-friendly defense
keyMatchups.body: Opponents send 28.4% of their targets to tight ends against New Orleans, above the league share. The Saints allow +0.35 EPA per play to the top tight end. Fannin is Watson's most efficient target by a distance, so feeding him is the clean route to scoring drives.

nextGame.watch: How often he throws beyond 10 yards: against this secondary, a plan that stays short wastes his best matchup of the year.

restOfSeason.body:
The underlying passer is roughly league-average: decent accuracy, a low interception rate and real efficiency when he throws past the sticks. The sacks are structural, a career trait behind the league's worst protection. So expect EPA per dropback to hover around average to slightly below, with sack totals near 4 a game unless the line improves. Yardage should stay steady at roughly 225-265 per game because the volume and short completions are reliable.

The touchdown rate is the likeliest thing to move up. Zero over three games sits poorly with his red-zone accuracy, so something in the 0.8-1.4 per game range is reasonable rather than the recent goose egg. Scrambles should keep his rushing at 15-30 yards a game, though designed runs will keep failing. The upside case requires the offense to lean on the intermediate game and Fannin. The downside case is another run of 8-sack games against strong fronts.

confidence.note: Eight starts, and the sack problem matches his career profile, but the downfield efficiency rests on only 65 attempts of 10+ air yards.
